chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Any free woman who marries herself to a slave without the permission of his masters has made her private part permissible [for sexual relations], and she has no dowry.'

key_terms.أَبَاحَتْ فَرْجَهَا: she made her private part permissible
key_terms.امْرَأَةٍ حُرَّةٍ: free woman (as opposed to a slave woman)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal consequence for a free woman who marries a slave without her master's permission?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith establishes the condition of *idhn al-awliya* (permission of guardians) for the validity of a free woman’s marriage to a slave, reflecting the classical juristic view that such unions require the master's consent due to the slave's limited legal autonomy. The ruling that she 'forfeits her dowry' (*la saqa laha*) implies that the marriage remains valid but lacks the full financial compensation typically due, while 'her private part becomes permissible' confirms the legitimacy of conjugal relations despite the procedural irregularity. This narration is pivotal in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between the validity of the contract (*sihha*) and the completeness of its rights (*kamal*).
